solutions.latex:
$x$-coordinate of $L$: $ax+3=0$, $x=-\dfrac{3}{a}$

$x$-coordinate of $M$: $bx+2=0$, $x=-\dfrac{2}{b}$

$$\begin{aligned}\therefore LM&=-\dfrac{2}{b}-\left(-\dfrac{3}{a}\right)\\&=-\dfrac{2}{b}+\dfrac{3}{a}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{cases}-\dfrac{2}{b}+\dfrac{3}{a}=5\\ab=-1\end{cases}\Rightarrow\begin{cases}3b-2a=5ab\\ab=-1\end{cases}\Rightarrow\begin{cases}3b-2a=-5\\ab=-1\end{cases}\Rightarrow\begin{cases}3b-2a=-5 & \ldots(1)\\a=-\dfrac{1}{b} & \ldots(2)\end{cases}$$

Sub (2) into (1):

$$\begin{aligned}3b-2\left(-\dfrac{1}{b}\right)&=-5\\3b+\dfrac{2}{b}&=-5\\3b^2+5b+2&=0\\(b+1)(3b+2)&=0\end{aligned}$$

$b=-1$ or $b=-\dfrac{2}{3}$

$\therefore\begin{cases}a=1\\b=-1\end{cases}$ or $\begin{cases}a=\dfrac{3}{2}\\b=-\dfrac{2}{3}\end{cases}$

Since $a>1$, $a+b=\dfrac{3}{2}-\dfrac{2}{3}=\dfrac{5}{6}$.

$\therefore\ D$

\exfigure{1373_q29_s1}

Find $x$-intercept: let $2\sqrt{x-1}=0$, $\sqrt{x-1}=0$, $x=1$

$x=10$: $y=2\sqrt{9}=6$

Area rectangle $=10\times 6=60$

$$\begin{aligned}A&=60-2\int_1^{10}\sqrt{x-1}\,dx\\&=60-2\int_1^{10}(x-1)^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dx\\&=60-2\left[\dfrac{2}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}\right]_1^{10}\\&=60-\dfrac{4}{3}(27-0)\\&=24\text{ u}^2\end{aligned}$$

Alternative solution:

$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{y}{2}&=\sqrt{x-1}\\x-1&=\dfrac{y^2}{4}\\x&=\dfrac{y^2}{4}+1\\A&=\int_0^6\left(\dfrac{y^2}{4}+1\right)dy\\&=\left[\dfrac{y^3}{12}+y\right]_0^6\\&=24\text{ u}^2\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}A&=49(\sin\theta+\sin\theta\cos\theta)\\A'&=49(\cos\theta+\cos\theta\cos\theta-\sin\theta\sin\theta)\\&=49(\cos\theta+\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta)\\A''&=49(-\sin\theta-2\cos\theta\sin\theta-2\sin\theta\cos\theta)\\&=49(-\sin\theta-4\sin\theta\cos\theta)\end{aligned}$$

For max or min, $A'=0$:

$$\begin{aligned}\cos\theta+\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta&=0\\\cos\theta+\cos^2\theta-(1-\cos^2\theta)&=0\\2\cos^2\theta+\cos\theta-1&=0\\2\cos^2\theta+2\cos\theta-\cos\theta-1&=0\\2\cos\theta(\cos\theta+1)-(\cos\theta+1)&=0\\(2\cos\theta-1)(\cos\theta+1)&=0\end{aligned}$$

$\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}$ or $\cos\theta=-1$; $\theta\ne\pi$ as $\theta$ must be acute

$\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Test: $$\begin{aligned}A''&=49\left(-\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}-4\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\\&=49\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-4\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right)=49\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)=-\dfrac{147\sqrt{3}}{2}<0\end{aligned}$$
